items.stem: Why is sound called a mechanical wave?
items.answer: It needs a material medium, and travels by the vibration of the particles of that medium.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: needs medium. 1 mark: particles vibrate.

items.answer: Too much reverberation from repeated reflections. Use curtains or fibreboard panels on walls, carpets on the floor, cushioned seats and perforated false ceilings to absorb sound.

items.stem:

items.answer: 1.7 m and 0.425 m; the 800 Hz sound has the higher pitch.
items.markingKey: λ = v/f: 340/200 = 1.7 m; 340/800 = 0.425 m. Higher frequency, higher pitch.

items.stem: Two sounds of 500 Hz and 1000 Hz travel through air (v = 340 m/s). Find both wavelengths and state which sound has the higher pitch.
items.answer: 0.68 m and 0.34 m; the 1000 Hz sound has the higher pitch.
items.markingKey: λ = v/f: 340/500 = 0.68 m; 340/1000 = 0.34 m. Higher frequency, higher pitch.

items.stem: A sound wave travels 1.5 km in sea water in 1 s. Its frequency is 1500 Hz. Find its wavelength. If the same source is sounded in air (344 m/s), what will be the new wavelength and will the pitch change?
items.answer: In water λ = 1500/1500 = 1 m. In air λ = 344/1500 = 0.229 m. Frequency (and so pitch) stays the same; only speed and wavelength change.

Why does the speed of sound in air increase on a hot day?
items.answer: The speed of sound in a gas increases with temperature, because faster-moving particles pass on the disturbance more quickly.

items.stem: Describe the structure and working of the human ear with a labelled diagram.
items.answer: Outer ear (pinna and ear canal) collects sound; the eardrum vibrates with compressions and rarefactions; the middle ear bones (hammer, anvil, stirrup) amplify the vibrations and pass them to the inner ear; the cochlea converts them into electrical signals that the auditory nerve carries to the brain.
items.markingKey: 1 mark outer; 2 marks middle; 2 marks inner.

items.stem: A sound has a frequency of 500 Hz. Is it infrasound, audible sound or ultrasound?

A stone is dropped into a 44.1 m deep well and the splash is heard 3.13 s later. Find the speed of sound (g = 9.8 m/s²).
items.answer: Fall time: h = ½gt², t = √(2 × 44.1/9.8) = 3 s. Sound takes 0.13 s, so v = 44.1/0.13 ≈ 339 m/s.
items.markingKey: 1 mark fall time. 1 mark sound time. 1 mark speed.
